title: contributor page about texts — our versioned words that explain Purpose Source on a contributor page
description:
The words of the about block of a contributor page (ops decision D163 and its dated notes of 2026-10-16; design contributor-publicity/D163-ABOUT-TEXTS-2026-10-16, version 2 of the texts and the technical map): the block a person keeps on, by default, first under their page's header, so a visitor reads the work listed below with its meaning. For each of our three texts, `short`, `medium` and `long`, a heading and its paragraphs; the proof sentence's frame and its noun forms; the invite's two forms; the line and heading that frame a person's own words (`own`); and the words and paths of the block's links. Plain text only: no markup, no Markdown, never a link but the two this file names; every renderer escapes it.

ONE PUBLICATION, PINNED BY HASH. The texts are published once, as `examples/contributor-page-about.v1.example.json` in this repository, and that file IS the texts, byte for byte, as `link-platforms.v1`'s example is the link table. The platform vendors it at `packages/contracts/data/contributor-page-about.v1.json` (the api stamps `current` into a person's settings at every save, and the page editor shows each text from it), and the website edge vendors it for the renderer; each pins its SHA-256.

APPEND-ONLY, SO A PUBLISHED PAGE KEEPS ITS WORDS. `versions` holds every version from 1 to `current`, in order, none missing. A version's words never change once it is published: each entry carries `sha256`, the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 (JCS) text of the entry without its `sha256` member, and `check:contributor-page` holds every entry to its recorded digest. New words are a new version: the api stamps the new `current` into a draft at its next save (and a draft it reads, so the editor previews the current words), while a published version keeps the version it was published with in `contributor-page-settings.v1` `about.version`, and its document is rebuilt with those words until its holder publishes again (`contributor-page.v1` `about.version`). A renderer without the version a document names leaves the block out rather than draw other words.

HOW THE BLOCK IS DRAWN FROM OUR TEXTS (`short`, `medium`, `long`). The heading, then the paragraphs in order, then the closing: the proof sentence and the invite, each written only where the rules below give one, joined by one space. `closing` says where they go: `same-paragraph` appends them to the last paragraph after one space (Short and Medium), `own-paragraph` makes them a paragraph of their own after the last (Long). With neither, nothing is added.

THE PROOF SENTENCE, composed at every render from the document the page is drawn from, so it never claims more than the page shows. Its parts, from `contributor-page.v1`: C, the `certificates` section lists at least one item whose `status` is `valid` or `expired` (revoked and superseded items never count; nC is their number); P, the document has a `repositories` section (nP is the number of rows across its groups); Q, the document has no `repositories` section but its `summary` section carries `projects` (the visitor finds a count, not the projects; a summary's certificate count never makes C); A, the document has an `adopter` section (nA is its number of items). P and Q never occur together. Each part's noun is `proof.nouns`' member of the section it is read from: `certificates` for C, `repositories` for P, `summary` for Q, `adopter` for A, the `one` form where its count is 1 and the `other` form otherwise (Q has one form). The parts are always in the order C, then P or Q, then A; two are joined with `proof.and`, three with `proof.comma` then `proof.and` (no serial comma). The list replaces `{list}` in `proof.frame`. With none of C, P, Q or A, there is no proof sentence.

THE INVITE. `invite.withCertificates` where the proof sentence names C (its "too" tells the visitor the holder has certificates), `invite.withoutCertificates` otherwise; `{link}` is `invite.link.words`, linked to the site's origin followed by `invite.link.path`. It is the block's last sentence and its only link. It is WITHHELD where certificates are not issued on the document's plane, because "you can earn" is not yet true there: on production (`contributor-page.v1` `source` is `platform`) until ops decision D160 item 8 opens certificates there, and on a public sample (`source` `sample`), which every site build draws, production's included, so it follows production; a renderer knows the plane as it knows it for its test band, and `examples/contributor-page-about.v1.golden.json` `certificatesIssued` names each plane. A block without the invite ends with `learnMore`'s words, linked to the site's origin followed by its `path`, so it never ends without a link.

THE PERSON'S OWN WORDS (`own`). `own.heading`, then the person's text exactly as the document carries it (`contributor-page.v1` `about.text`: line breaks kept, never turned into links), then `own.line` followed by `learnMore`'s link. No proof sentence and no invite: those are the holder's own words.

THE `lint` MEMBER is never drawn. It carries the copy-lint allow markers of this repository (on its line) and of the website (counted per file) for the one deliberate mention of the predecessor in each text (ops decision D25: mentioned as the predecessor, never a descriptor of Purpose Source), which is why it shares the line of the paragraph that holds the mention.

x-psn.phase: P-M3 (with the contributor page). Nothing reads it yet: the api's save (which stamps `current`), the page editor's four choices (CW-38) and the edge renderer's about block (D163 item 6) are built against it.
x-psn.artifactPath: (this repository) examples/contributor-page-about.v1.example.json — the texts themselves, byte for byte; vendored byte-identically by the platform (packages/contracts/data/contributor-page-about.v1.json) and the website edge, each pinning its SHA-256
x-psn.producer: authored in this repository by the orchestrator (D163 item 6), claim-checked against the licence summary, the statutes and the claim-language kit before each version is published (D163 item 3)
consumers: the api, which stamps `current` into `contributor-page-settings.v1` `about.version` at every save
the page editor, which shows each of the three texts and the own-words framing from `current` (CW-38)
the website edge renderer, which draws the about block of `contributor-page.v1` with the version the document names
fsRefs: D163 items 1 to 5, and its dated notes of 2026-10-16T19:52Z and ~20:50Z
D163-ABOUT-TEXTS-2026-10-16 (version 2: the texts, the proof sentence's composition, the invite; the technical map)
D160 items 1, 3 and 8 (the invite's two forms, and where it is withheld)
D25 (the predecessor may be mentioned, never used as a descriptor)

current.description: The version the api stamps into a person's settings at every save, and the editor shows: the last entry of `versions`.

versions.description: Every version from 1 to `current`, in order; append-only.

from.description: The UTC day the version was written.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 text of this entry without its `sha256` member.

short.description: Short: one paragraph, a few sentences.

long.description: Long: the whole story in a short read, several paragraphs.

proof.description: The proof sentence's frame and nouns (see the description).

certificates.description: C: the certificates section lists one or more valid or expired items.

repositories.description: P: the repositories section is present.

summary.description: Q: no repositories section, and the summary carries the projects count; one form for any count.

adopter.description: A: the adopter section is present.

invite.description: The invite's two fixed forms (see the description).

own.description: What frames the person's own words: the heading above them, and our one line after them, followed by `learnMore`'s link.

learnMore.description: The link after the own words' line, and the block's last words wherever the invite is withheld.

lint.description: Never drawn: the copy-lint allow markers for the paragraph on its line (see the description).

closing.description: Where the proof sentence and the invite go: appended to the last paragraph after one space, or a paragraph of their own after it.

other.description: Where the count is anything else.

path.description: A path on the site's own origin: the renderer prefixes the origin it draws every site link with.
